feed.title: THE 7 MOST POPULAR BLOCKERS ALREADY ANSWERED
feed.body:
1. "...if I had more time" ⏰.                                                                             
You don't need 20 hours. You need 40 focused minutes and a phone.

The scroll you're doing right now is the time. It just isn't pointed at anything yet.


2.  "...if I knew what to sell" 🎯

Tell Claude what people thank you for and it will hand you five product ideas in one minute.

Not knowing is a 10-minute problem people treat like a 10-year one.


3.  "...if I wasn't afraid of looking dumb" 😬

Start a page that isn't your name. Nobody you know sees it.

Judgment-proof. Test everything in private, tell people after it works.


4. "...if I had money to start" 💵

A Facebook page is free. Claude costs less than dinner. A payment link is free.

The broke excuse died a few years ago. Quietly. Nobody sent the memo.


5. "...if I knew it would work" 🎲

Nobody knows. I didn't know. Certainty arrives AFTER the reps, never before.

What's YOUR blank? Drop it below. If it's not in my seven, I'll answer it personally.

feed.title: Google Gemini is WAY more powerful than most people realize.
feed.body:
Most users are only scratching the surface.
Here are 6 underrated Gemini features that can save you time, boost your productivity, and completely change how you use AI. 👇

📌 Save this post—you’ll want to come back to it.

1️⃣ DEEP RESEARCH MODE

Stop spending hours digging through sources manually. 🔎

Gemini’s Deep Research can turn a simple topic into a structured, citation-backed research report.

Just open Gemini → choose “3.1 Pro with Deep Research” from the model menu → enter your topic.

Gemini can:
• Search across dozens of sources
• Cross-check key findings
• Organize information into a structured report
• Provide citations for your sources
• Save you hours of manual research

It feels less like chatting with an AI—and more like having a research assistant working alongside you.

⚡ What could take hours of searching and summarizing can be condensed into a much faster workflow.

The result? A polished starting point for research, analysis, content creation, or decision-making.

🚀 One prompt. Deep research. A complete report.


2️⃣ GEMS: YOUR CUSTOM AI ASSISTANTS

Why repeat the same instructions every time you use AI?

Gems let you build your own specialized AI assistants—each designed for a specific task, workflow, or role.

Open Gemini → Sidebar → Gems → Create New

You can create a Gem for almost anything:

🐍 Python Tutor — adapts explanations to your learning style.
✍️ Writing Assistant — writes in your preferred tone and style.
📈 Business Coach — helps analyze ideas and build strategies.
🍽️ Meal Planner — follows your chosen preferences and requirements.

The real advantage? ⚡

Your Gem keeps its custom instructions, role, and purpose ready to use.

No more starting every chat with:

“Act as…”
“Remember this…”
“Use this tone…”

Set it up once, then let your specialized AI assistant handle the rest.

🚀 Think of Gems as your personal team of AI specialists—built in minutes.





3️⃣ CONNECT GEMINI TO YOUR GMAIL, DRIVE & CALENDAR

This is where Gemini starts feeling less like a chatbot—and more like a personal productivity assistant. ⚡

Go to Settings → Apps and connect the Google services available to you, such as Gmail, Drive, Calendar, Maps, and YouTube.

Once connected, Gemini can help you work across your Google ecosystem.

Try prompts like:

📧 “Summarize the emails my boss sent this week.”
📁 “Find the Q3 presentation I worked on last month.”
📅 “What meetings do I have next Tuesday?”
▶️ “Find the marketing video I watched recently.”

Instead of jumping between emails, files, folders, and apps, you can ask Gemini in natural language and let it help you find, summarize, and organize information faster.

🚀 That’s the real shift: Gemini becomes part of your workflow—not just another chatbot.



4️⃣ LIVE VOICE CONVERSATIONS

Stop typing. Just talk to Gemini. 🎙️

Open the Gemini app → tap the microphone → start speaking naturally.

This isn’t simple voice dictation.

With Gemini Live, you can have a real-time conversation, ask follow-up questions, change direction, and build on the context as you talk.

You can:

🗣️ Interrupt naturally
🔄 Switch topics instantly
💡 Brainstorm ideas hands-free
🎯 Ask follow-up questions without restarting

Use it to:

• Generate content ideas while walking
• Draft emails without touching your keyboard
• Explore a topic while multitasking
• Practice interviews in real time
• Turn scattered thoughts into clear action plans

The experience feels much closer to talking with an AI assistant than using a traditional chatbot.

🤯 Sometimes, the fastest way to use AI is simply to talk.




5️⃣ AI IMAGE GENERATION BUILT INTO GEMINI

You don’t need a separate image tool for every visual task. 🎨

Just tell Gemini what you want:

“Generate an image of…” + your idea.

Gemini can create visuals for:

📸 Photorealistic scenes
📦 Product mockups
🎬 Cinematic concepts
📱 Social media graphics
📢 Ad creatives
✍️ Images featuring text and typography

And the workflow stays inside the same conversation.

No jumping between apps.
No complicated workflow.
Just describe → generate → refine.

You can also upload an existing image and use natural-language instructions to edit it:

• “Remove the background.”
• “Change the shirt color to black.”
• “Replace the coffee cup with a laptop.”
• “Turn this into a cinematic poster.”

🔥 Generate. Edit. Refine. All from one conversation.

That’s what makes Gemini’s image capabilities so useful for creators, marketers, and everyday users.





5️⃣ AI IMAGE GENERATION BUILT INTO GEMINI

Gemini isn’t just for generating images—it can help you create, edit, and refine visuals in the same conversation. 🎨

Create:

• Images with clear, readable text
• Cinematic scenes
• Scroll-stopping social media visuals
• Professional ad creatives

The biggest advantage?

Everything happens in one conversation.

No jumping between apps.
No complicated workflows.
No separate editing process.

And it gets even more powerful. 👇

Upload an existing image and edit it with simple prompts:

• “Remove the background.”
• “Change the shirt color to black.”
• “Replace the coffee cup with a laptop.”
• “Turn this into a cinematic poster.”

🔥 Generate → Edit → Refine.

One conversation. One workflow. Endless creative possibilities.

No camera.
No face.
No complicated editing.

Just Claude, the right prompts, and a repeatable workflow for creating Shorts faster.
I’m sharing the 12 exact prompts you can use to build, script, optimize, and scale your Shorts. 👇

Save this. You’ll want these later.

1. 90% fail by choosing the wrong niche.

Prompt:

"I am [AGE] years old and interested in [TOPICS].

Give me the 5 Shorts niches with the highest CPM.

Include: competition, actual revenue at 10K subs, and which one to start TODAY with no money.

Order by monetization speed."




2. A short without a script is a dead short.

Prompt:

"Write a 45-second short script about [TOPIC] for [AUDIENCE].

Include:

Hook in the first 3 seconds

3 key points with facts

Final CTA that generates comments

Conversational tone, short sentences."



3. If you lose the viewer in 3 seconds, you lose everything.

Prompt:

"Give me 20 one-line hooks for a Short about

[TOPIC].

5 of curiosity. 5 of shock. 5 of direct question.

5 of brutal promise.

Each hook must have fewer than 10 words and sound like something a real human.



4. The title decides whether they open you or ignore you.

Prompt:

"Generate 15 titles for a Short about [TOPIC].

5 with numbers. 5 with questions. 5 with emotional tension.

Less than 60 characters.

Add which one has the most viral potential and why."




Y
5. You don't need your voice. Nor to appear on camera.

Prompt:

"Adapt this script for Al-generated voice-over (ElevenLabs or similar).

Mark pauses with [...], emphasis with UPPERCASE and emotion between parentheses.

Script:

[PASTE YOUR SCRIPT]"


6. The algorithm rewards those who stay until the end.

Prompt:

"Restructure this script for maximum retention in Shorts.

Add:

Loop at the beginning and end

Cliffhanger at 15s

Unexpected twist at 30s

Give me the second-by-second optimized version."



7. Your description is free SEO. Most people waste it.

Prompt:

"Create the perfect description for a Short on [TOPIC].

Include:

First line with exact keyword

3 hook lines

15 hashtags (5 big, 5 medium, 5 niche)"




8. The problem isn't making 1 short. It's making 100.

Prompt:

"Give me 30 short ideas about [NICHE] for the next 30 days.

Each idea with:

Title

1-line hook

Unique angle

Don't repeat concepts. Mix educational, viral, and controversial




9. 1 long video = 10 shorts.

Prompt:

Analyze this long script and extract 10 independent shorts.

Each with:

Own hook

Closed beginning and end

Between 30 and 60 seconds

Script: [PASTE YOUR CONTENT]''


10. AdSense is the beginning. Not the end.

Prompt:

"I'm a creator of Shorts about [NICHE] with [X] subscribers.

Give me 7 ways to monetize right now.

Order by: realistic first-month revenue + ease of implementation.

No theory. Concrete examples."




11. Don't invent the wheel. Copy what already works.

Prompt:

"Analyze these 5 Shorts channels about

[NICHE]: [NAMES].

Give me:

Common pattern in their hooks

Structure of their titles

What the ones growing fastest do differently

3 gaps I can exploit"




12. Posting whenever you feel like it = algorithm against you.

Prompt:

"Create a 30-day posting calendar for a Shorts channel about [NICHE].

Include:

Best time according to time zone [YOUR ZONE]

Optimal frequency

Mix of formats per week"
feed.title: CLAUDE + YOUTUBE SHORTS = A POWERFUL CONTENT  ENGINE.

feed.body:
NotebookLM turns your sources into research you can actually trust.
Then ChatGPT turns that research into posts, scripts, visuals, content plans, and repeatable workflows.
Here is the full content system 👇🏽


STEP 1: Understand The System
Most creators use ChatGPT like this:
“Give me 10 content ideas.”
That is why the output feels generic.
The better workflow:
NotebookLM = your research brain.
ChatGPT = your content execution engine.
NotebookLM helps you understand the sources.
ChatGPT turns the useful insights into posts, scripts, visuals, calendars, and repeatable systems.
The goal is simple:
Stop creating from random ideas.
Start creating from organized research.



STEP 2: Build One Notebook Around Your Niche
Open NotebookLM and create one notebook for the topic you want to become known for.
Upload useful sources:
• YouTube videos
• PDFs
• reports
• articles
• websites
• customer questions
• competitor content
• your own notes
• research papers
• audio files
Do not upload random information.
Choose sources your audience would actually care about.
Then ask:
“Analyze these sources and identify:
1. the biggest problems people are trying to solve
2. the questions that appear repeatedly
3. the most surprising insights
4. common mistakes
5. useful frameworks
6. strong opinions or debates
7. topics people misunderstand
8. practical actions someone could take today
Organize the findings into clear sections.
Focus on useful content opportunities, not generic summaries.”



STEP 3: Turn The Research Into Content Pillars
Once NotebookLM understands the sources, do not ask for random post ideas yet.
First, build the map.
Use this prompt inside NotebookLM:
“Turn these sources into 5 clear content pillars.
For each pillar, give me:
1. the main audience problem
2. why people care about it
3. the most useful insights from the sources
4. beginner questions
5. advanced questions
6. common mistakes
7. myths worth correcting
8. practical examples
9. 10 content angles
10. the sources supporting the pillar
Make the pillars different enough that the content does not feel repetitive.”
You can also generate a Mind Map to see how the ideas connect.
This gives you structure before you create anything.




STEP 4: Create A Research Brief You Can Reuse
Now ask NotebookLM to turn the - into one clean document.
Use this:
“Create a content research brief from these sources.
Include:
1. target audience problems
2. recurring questions
3. strongest insights
4. useful statistics or facts
5. surprising findings
6. myths to challenge
7. examples or case studies
8. content pillars
9. 30 possible topics
10. source references for important claims
Keep the brief clear and practical.
Write it so another content strategist could use it without reading every source.”
Save the response as a note.
This becomes the source material for ChatGPT.



STEP 5: Create A ChatGPT Project For Your Brand
Open ChatGPT and create a Project for the page, business, or client.
Add:
• the NotebookLM research brief
• your audience description
• your tone of voice
• your best previous posts
• your content rules
• examples you like
• topics to avoid
• your posting frequency
• your main goal
Then add this instruction:
“You are my content strategist.
Use the uploaded research and brand files as the foundation for every answer.
Do not generate generic ideas.
Prioritize:
1. specific audience problems
2. useful outcomes
3. strong hooks
4. simple language
5. fresh angles
6. accurate claims
7. content people would save or share
When an idea is weak, say so clearly and replace it with a stronger one.”
Now ChatGPT is not starting from zero every time.



STEP 6: Build A Content Bank From The Research
Inside the ChatGPT Project, use this:
“Use the uploaded research brief to create a content bank.
Give me:
1. 30 text-post ideas
2. 20 Reel ideas
3. 10 carousel ideas
4. 10 visual infographic ideas
5. 10 opinion posts
6. 10 mistakes-to-avoid posts
7. 10 step-by-step guides
8. 10 beginner-friendly ideas
9. 10 advanced ideas
10. 10 sequel ideas based on the strongest topics
For every idea, include:
• the hook
• the audience problem
• the useful takeaway
• the best format
• the CTA
• the content pillar
Rank the top 20 ideas by potential.
Avoid repeating the same angle with slightly different words.”
This gives you a real content library instead of one random calendar.



STEP 7: Turn One Idea Into A Complete Content Package
Once you choose an idea, do not ask for only one caption.
Use this:
“Turn this idea into a complete content package:
[INSERT IDEA]
Create:
1. 10 hook options
2. the strongest hook and why it works
3. the full Facebook text post
4. a comment thread with real value
5. a 45-second Reel script
6. a carousel slide structure
7. a visual-generation prompt
8. a short version for X
9. a LinkedIn version
10. 3 sequel ideas
11. one pinned comment
12. one CTA
Rules:
• keep the language simple
• avoid empty hype
• avoid robotic phrasing
• make the value clear quickly
• keep claims accurate
• make every version feel native to the platform”
One researched idea can become an entire content campaign.




STEP 8: Use ChatGPT Images For The Visuals
You do not need to open another tool for every visual idea.
Ask ChatGPT to turn the post into a clear visual concept.
Use this:
“Create 5 visual concepts for this post:
[PASTE POST]
For each concept, give me:
1. the main visual idea
2. why it would stop the scroll
3. the subject
4. the background
5. the composition
6. the emotional expression
7. the text overlay, if needed
8. the exact image-generation prompt
Keep the designs simple.
Use one clear focal point.
Avoid crowded layouts, tiny text, and generic AI visuals.
Rank the concepts from strongest to weakest.”
Then generate the strongest concept and refine it.



STEP 9: Turn Winners Into A Repeatable System
The best creators do not start from zero every day.
After publishing, paste your results into ChatGPT:
“Analyze these posts:
[PASTE POSTS WITH REACH, LIKES, COMMENTS, SHARES, SAVES, AND CLICKS]
Tell me:
1. which topics worked best
2. which hooks worked best
3. which formats worked best
4. which posts generated the most shares
5. which posts generated the most useful engagement
6. what patterns appear across the winners
7. what I should stop posting
8. what I should double down on
9. 20 new ideas based on the strongest patterns
10. 5 experiments for next week
Do not only rank the posts.
Explain why the winners worked.”
Then send the strongest topics back into NotebookLM and research them more deeply.
That is how the system improves every week.



STEP 10: Add Optional Automation
Once the manual system works, make it easier to repeat.
Inside ChatGPT, create a recurring Task:
“Every Sunday, remind me to review my content performance.
Ask me to paste the weekly numbers.
Then help me identify the winners, the weak posts, and the 10 strongest ideas for the next week.”
You can also use agent mode for multi-step work when it is available on your plan.
Examples:
• researching a topic across websites
• organizing files
• collecting useful information
• helping prepare a report
• completing a longer online task with your approval
Do not automate a weak workflow.
Build the system manually first.
Automate only after you know what works.

Create a new notebook in NotebookLM and add the material you want to use:
• PDFs, ebooks, or research papers.
• Notes, scripts, or text files.
• Web sources using NotebookLM’s search feature when you don’t have a document ready.

2. Set the language first 

Open the settings and choose your preferred output language before generating the video.

This helps ensure the narration and generated content match the language you want.


3. Pick your video format 

Open Video Overview and choose the format that fits your content.

• Short Video — ideal for Shorts, Reels, and TikTok.
• Cinematic Explainer — better suited for longer, landscape-style educational content.

4. Use these custom prompt templates

Choose Custom Topic instead of relying entirely on the default options. Give NotebookLM a clear idea of what you want emphasized.

▪︎ Educational explainer: 
Prompt > "Explain the main ideas from this source in a fast, engaging video. Use simple visual animations and motion graphics to make [TOPIC] easy to understand. Prioritize clarity and visually simplify complex information.”

▪︎ Story-driven: 
Prompt > “Turn this source into a compelling narrative about [TOPIC]. Start with a strong hook, build curiosity throughout the video, and use cinematic visuals to highlight the most important discoveries and conclusions.”

▪︎ Step-by-step tutorial: 
Prompt > "Create a practical instructional video based on this source. Present [PROCESS] as clear visual steps and focus on helping the viewer achieve [OUTCOME]. Keep each stage simple and easy to follow.”


5. Review before publishing 

Always preview the generated video.
AI-generated visuals can sometimes misrepresent diagrams, data, or technical details, so verify the important sections before publishing.

For content in languages other than English, also check the captions carefully. If they need correction, you can add accurate subtitles afterward using a video editor.
